scenes.heading: Helm & Kubernetes Packaging
scenes.narration: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes, letting you template, version, and release complex applications as a single unit.

scenes.heading: What Helm provides
bullets: Rollback returns to a previous release instantly
scenes.narration: A Helm chart bundles all the related manifests for an application into one package. Templates let you parameterize values so the same chart serves development and production with different settings. Each install becomes a tracked release with a version history. And if something goes wrong, a single command rolls the release back to a previous known-good state.

scenes.heading: Raw manifests vs Helm charts
scenes.narration: Managing raw YAML means copying and pasting manifests for each environment, which quickly drifts out of sync and offers no release history. A Helm chart replaces that with one templated definition driven by per-environment values files, keeping things clean and giving you versioned releases you can roll back.

scenes.heading: A templated deployment
scenes.code:
# templates/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-etl
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: etl
          image: "{{ .Values.image.repo }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"

# values.yaml
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repo: myrepo/etl
  tag: "1.4.0"
scenes.narration: The template uses double-brace placeholders that Helm fills in at install time. The release name and replica count come from Helm's built-in objects and your values file. The image repository and tag are also externalized into values, so promoting a new version to production is as simple as changing the tag value rather than editing the template itself.

scenes.heading: The Helm release workflow
scenes.narration: Running helm install kicks things off. Helm renders the templates by merging them with your values. It then applies the resulting manifests to the cluster as a named release. Later you upgrade to ship new versions, or roll back instantly if a release misbehaves.

scenes.text: Helm turns Kubernetes deployments into versioned, parameterized packages you can install, upgrade, and roll back with one command.
scenes.narration: Think of Helm as turning your Kubernetes deployments into versioned, parameterized packages that you can install, upgrade, and roll back with a single command.
